node.label: US politics & midterms
node.summary: US elections and how foreign policy plays at home.

facts.text: US Vice-President **J.D. Vance** blamed the **Iran war** for the Republican midterm defeat ('The reason we lost is the war'), positioning himself as the front-runner for the **2028** Republican presidential nomination.
facts.plain: US Vice-President J.D. Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican midterm defeat ('The reason we lost is the war'), positioning himself as the front-runner for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination.

facts.text: President **Donald Trump** congratulated Democrats on the result, conceded the **Iran war** 'played a part' in Republican losses, but denied personal responsibility and warned he would **veto** Democratic bills.
facts.plain: President Donald Trump congratulated Democrats on the result, conceded the Iran war 'played a part' in Republican losses, but denied personal responsibility and warned he would veto Democratic bills.

facts.text: Democrats now hold at least **28 of 50** US governorships (up from 24); **Gina Hinojosa** became Texas's first Democratic Governor since **1995**, unseating **Greg Abbott**; **Keisha Lance Bottoms** became Georgia's first Black woman Governor.
facts.plain: Democrats now hold at least 28 of 50 US governorships (up from 24); Gina Hinojosa became Texas's first Democratic Governor since 1995, unseating Greg Abbott; Keisha Lance Bottoms became Georgia's first Black woman Governor.

facts.text: US midterm 'firsts': **James Talarico** — first Democrat to win Texas statewide office in decades (beating AG **Ken Paxton**); **Adam Hamilton** — first Democratic Kansas senator since **1932**; **Annie Andrews** — first Democratic South Carolina senator since **1998**; **Abdul El-Sayed** (Michigan) — first Muslim elected to the US Senate.
facts.plain: US midterm 'firsts': James Talarico — first Democrat to win Texas statewide office in decades (beating AG Ken Paxton); Adam Hamilton — first Democratic Kansas senator since 1932; Annie Andrews — first Democratic South Carolina senator since 1998; Abdul El-Sayed (Michigan) — first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

facts.text: In the 4 Nov US midterms, Democrats won control of both chambers: at least **237 of 435** House seats (analysts project 250+) and at least **54 of 100** Senate seats (incl. 2 independents), flipping **7** Republican-held Senate seats — **Texas, Ohio, South Carolina, Iowa, Maine, North Carolina, Kansas**.
facts.plain: In the 4 Nov US midterms, Democrats won control of both chambers: at least 237 of 435 House seats (analysts project 250+) and at least 54 of 100 Senate seats (incl. 2 independents), flipping 7 Republican-held Senate seats — Texas, Ohio, South Carolina, Iowa, Maine, North Carolina, Kansas.

facts.text: US **midterm elections** (3 Nov): all **435** House seats, **35 of 100** Senate seats and **36** Governorships were at stake; Republicans held the Senate **53-47**. Trump's approval was near the low 30s.
facts.plain: US midterm elections (3 Nov): all 435 House seats, 35 of 100 Senate seats and 36 Governorships were at stake; Republicans held the Senate 53-47. Trump's approval was near the low 30s.

facts.text: Kansas has not elected a Democratic senator since **1932**; the race is Roger Marshall vs Adam Hamilton.
facts.plain: Kansas has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932; the race is Roger Marshall vs Adam Hamilton.

facts.text: US **midterm elections** on 3 Nov 2026: tariffs and the Iran war (fuel prices) are key issues.
facts.plain: US midterm elections on 3 Nov 2026: tariffs and the Iran war (fuel prices) are key issues.

facts.text: Harvard's ElectIt model (Gary King et al.) forecast Democrats winning **230 of 435 House seats** and 18 of 35 contested Senate seats in the US midterms; President Trump's approval stood near 37% against ~60% disapproval, and the generic ballot showed Democrats leading 51%-42%.
facts.plain: Harvard's ElectIt model (Gary King et al.) forecast Democrats winning 230 of 435 House seats and 18 of 35 contested Senate seats in the US midterms; President Trump's approval stood near 37% against ~60% disapproval, and the generic ballot showed Democrats leading 51%-42%.

facts.text: Ahead of the 3 November US midterms, the Department of Justice pressured county election officials (e.g. Fulton County, Georgia) for voter-list data and warned all 50 States that failing to preserve election records risks up to a year in prison; a California federal judge rejected a DOJ subpoena for ~20,000 ballots on 28 October.

facts.text: The US plans to deport over **150 Afghans** via Pakistan, including relatives of Afghans who helped the US military.
facts.plain: The US plans to deport over 150 Afghans via Pakistan, including relatives of Afghans who helped the US military.

facts.text: AP-NORC poll (8-11 Oct): 85% of US voters rank the economy and 84% the cost of living among top issues; two-thirds disapprove of the military action in Iran (Pew).
facts.plain: AP-NORC poll (8-11 Oct): 85% of US voters rank the economy and 84% the cost of living among top issues; two-thirds disapprove of the military action in Iran (Pew).

facts.text: US Senate is **53-47** Republican; 35 seats are up. Cook Political Report lists 7 toss-ups (Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas). In Texas, **Ken Paxton** (R) faces **James Talarico** (D); **Elon Musk** gave $158 million indirectly for Paxton. Democrats need to flip **3** House seats.
